correctness.rationale: For every permitted finite graph and each real exponent, the complete zero-sum powered-distance form is derived from exact graph distances. Cauchy–Schwarz reduces it to a symmetric three-variable form; for exponents from zero through one the lower two-by-two block is positive definite by concavity of the power function. The explicit Schur complement has the asserted positive and nonpositive endpoint values. The finite-metric strictness interval gives the unique global critical root and excludes larger exponents. Critical corank is one. The balanced symmetry reduction, nonzero equality vector, and mean-value theorem prove monotonicity and the cubic asymptotic. The standalone checker independently passed 5,414 finite assertions; analytical proof, not testing, establishes all parameters.

value.rationale: The sharp Hilbert-snowflake exponent is a natural metric invariant. The exact two-parameter classification for an elementary single-edge perturbation fills a gap between published unpowered quadratic embedding and generic finite determinant methods. The one-dimensional critical null space identifies affine embedding dimension, and the balanced family has a strictly positive, quantitatively sharp inverse-cubic advantage with strict monotonicity. These are structural, not merely numerical or cosmetic, results.
